newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady to weak.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady to weak.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mostly steady to weaker on Monday as several dealers eyed rising corn prices on the Chicago Board of Trade.

"The move in corn has not done anything yet," a Kansas dealer said of any impact on the wheat middlings market. "I think everybody is just trying to wait to see if this board stays (high) even into tomorrow."

He added that high temperatures in Kansas and Oklahoma over the weekend dried pastures. "But it seems like nobody is ready to do anything yet. So as a consequence we are sitting here." The market is in the doldrums, he said.
When it is extremely hot as it has been, cattle do not eat a lot. They continue to graze on the grass that is out there even though the grass is drying out, the Kansas dealer said.
In Texas, the heat was also drying up pastures and nearby millfeed supplies remained tight, a north Texas dealer said.
Deliveries were the focal point, a North Carolina dealer said, referring to Monday's activity. "Everybody is just chasing trucks, trying to make sure they get there (destinations) today," he said.
He said soft red winter wheat in his area was being used by feed mixers in their ingredients.
"Wheat midds are cheap," the North Carolina dealer said.
